newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN RENAULT UNIONS AGREE PLANT CLOSURE DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN RENAULT UNIONS AGREE PLANT CLOSURE DEAL.

text.p: Unions at the Vilvoorde, Belgium, plant of French car maker Renault said on Wednesday they agreed on a package of social measures for the closure of the plant.
"On the jobs front we have secured 400 jobs with a Renault contract and 200 additional jobs on the Vilvoorde site with other companies," union leader Karel Gacoms told Belgian radio.
The deal was made after 15-hour talks in which Renault management threathened to let the Belgian unit go bankrupt if the unions did not accept the final offer.
The outline of the package was already agreed last week.
Renault said last week it planned to set up a new industrial activity at Vilvoorde that would keep on 400 staff of the 3,100 people employed there when it announced the closure in February.

Belgian media said Renault had agreed to guarantee employment for another 200 people at the Vilvoorde site, for which Renault will seek a new industrial operator. The 200 new jobs were the only new element in the deal outlined last week.
"We did not manage to get higher financial compensation," Gacoms said.
Renault last week proposed to give workers up to two years to find a job while remaining in "technical unemployment" on compensation of 43,000 francs a month.
A special unit would be set up to help them find work.
The deal also called for early retirement for 522 people between the ages of 48 and 50.
Workers taking redundancy would be offered cash bonuses averaging 900,000 Belgian francs and going as high as two million francs, depending on length of service.
On July 17 the deal will be presented to Renault workers who will vote on it a few days later.

Renault has not given an estimate for the total cost of the deal. The carmaker has set aside 2.8 billion French francs ($475 million) to pay for closing Vilvoorde, including the cost of a jobs and compensation package, reconstruction of the site and capital losses on investments.
